_README: The nine kinds of stage a level can be built from.
WRITTEN BY HAND. export_data.py never overwrites it. The canon stage
rows in stages.json are the workbook's; this file is the playtest's own
vocabulary, taken from Cameron's Levels Design Scheme of 2026-09-21.
A level names a type and overrides whatever it wants to differ - the
number of opponents, the threshold, the turn limit. Everything not
overridden comes from here, so 'the default committee is 60 votes' is
affinity_stage_id points at the canon stage whose suit multipliers and
audience mix this type borrows, so a press conference favours the same

committee_debate._shape: One committee member at a time. Each is a fresh argument: turns, gaffes and energy all start again. Fifteen turns, set by Cameron on 2026-09-21: at eight the stage measured 0 wins in 20 seeded runs, because reaching 60 means winning over every single undecided member and there is no slack in the clock to do it.

floor_debate._shape: One debater after another on one clock. Your record, your hand and the turns carry across all of them.

press_conference._shape: One question per turn. Energy comes back each turn; the hand does not.

party_caucus._shape: One bank of energy for the whole meeting. However high the room gets is the result.

town_hall._shape: Constituents one after another. The clock and your record carry; the energy does not - each new face is a fresh three.

media_ambush._shape: One reporter, no escape. One bank of energy for the whole thing, every gaffe counts double, and ducking a question ends it.

lobbyist_meeting._shape: Their interest cools while you talk. One bank of energy, and the clock is working against you.

policy_study._shape: Officials ask two questions a turn. Energy comes back each turn; the hand does not.

tv_debate._shape: Ten turns, ten points of energy, and three gaffes is the end of you. No refills either way.
tv_debate._note: Cameron's 2026-09-21 definition, which replaces the survival model in CLAUDE.md 7.3 for this stage.
